title: Seoul in 5 days: 15 stops for palaces, markets and food
desc: A five-day Seoul route covering palaces, hanok villages, markets and local food, organised day by day.

items.title: Nuldam Space, Gyeongbokgung (늘담 경복궁점)
items.memo: Cafe where you write a letter to your future self, mailed to you later.

items.title: Bukchon Hanok Village (북촌한옥마을)
items.memo: Hanok lanes open to visitors 10am-5pm; residents live here, so keep noise down.

items.title: Samcheongdong Sujebi (삼청동수제비)
items.memo: Michelin-listed hand-pulled dough soup and potato pancakes.

items.title: Oncheonjip (온천집)
items.memo: Shabu-shabu in an Ikseon-dong courtyard; reserve ahead.

items.title: Gwangjang Market (광장시장)
items.memo: Night food tour: about 2.5 hours and a dozen tastings.

items.title: Changdeokgung Palace (창덕궁)
items.memo: UNESCO palace from 1405; Secret Garden needs its own ticket.

items.title: Myeongdong Kyoja (명동교자 본점)
items.memo: Michelin-listed hand-cut noodle soup and dumplings.

items.title: Coffee Hanyakbang (커피한약방)
items.memo: Retro coffee shop tucked in an alley.

items.title: Namdaemun Market (남대문시장)
items.memo: Big, less touristy market; look for hotteok and wang mandu.

items.title: N Seoul Tower (N서울타워)
items.memo: Take the cable car up about two hours before sunset.

items.title: Starfield Library (별마당 도서관)
items.memo: Towering book walls inside COEX Mall; free, a quick stop if nearby.

items.title: Seoul Forest Park (서울숲)
items.memo: Large park next to Seongsu, good for a walk.
